# R403 v2 addendum: verifier-profile observer effects

Date: 2026-10-13. Source-only audit; canonical worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-gated-quality-capture-20261013` at clean commit `b4f7b5ec1d7583de52f0e0dbcf181d461591cf17`. No build, test, GPU, profiler, Git mutation, service action, cleanup, or source edit.

Correction to v1 wording: `profile_report()` was not newly added to ordinary serve and was not standalone-only in the inspected source. The ordinary serve `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` callsite was present in this exact canonical source (`src/program/generate.cpp:9717,10495-10518`); the earlier premise missed that callsite. V1's source coverage conclusion stands, but its description of the source as a “correction” to an outdated premise should be read as a correction of the audit premise, not a source change.

## Material route change under profiling

The profile is a treatment that changes execution policy, not just an observer on a fixed route. In `Verifier::record_window()` the dataflow mixer side branch is selected with:

`br = df_branch_ && G == 1 && !batch_rec_ && !prof_on_` (`src/core/verify.cpp:499-501`).

Thus, when the quiet effective `df_branch_` is true in a one-group, non-batched window, setting `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` forces `br=false`; the mixer operations that could fork to `df_side_` run on the main compute stream instead. The source comment identifies `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` as the control and says graph-branch benefit was device-dependent (RTX 4070 +0.7%, B70 -4%, from the comment's historical measurements), but neither value is a B570 measurement and neither identifies the effective setting for the exact quiet run of interest. If `df_branch_` was already false, this particular schedule change is absent. If `G != 1` or the window is batched, the branch is also unavailable independently of profiling.

The profile-mode device-stage ratios therefore describe the instrumented serial mixer schedule when the quiet one-group graph would otherwise branch. They cannot be applied as per-phase exclusive fractions, or assumed to rank the quiet execution path. Even when `df_branch_` was false, the extra profiling commands and copies remain observer effects requiring qualification.

## Other `prof_on_` guards inspected

- Initialization sets profiling from environment-variable presence, then clears it if the required device clock is unavailable or device allocation fails (`verify.cpp:368-378`). Consequently an environment variable alone does not prove stamps ran; only the per-request output / diagnostic that confirms profile lines is evidence of output. No B570 capability query was performed.
- The regular `stamp` lambda submits `gpu_stamp` at existing graph boundaries when `prof_on_ && grp==0` (`verify.cpp:506`; callsites across 571-1281). Those are additional device commands/nodes. The math input/output pointers are not changed by these calls, but no overhead or graph scheduling neutrality is established.
- The fused hyper-connection read receives a non-null stamp buffer only when `prof_on_ && grp==0` (`verify.cpp:674`). `fused_gr_read_multi` then submits two internal GPU stamps for its Q8 branch (or stamps around the non-Q8 path; `src/kernels/xe/fused_gr.cpp:180,276-277,619,658`). Its arithmetic route appears unchanged in source; command count and measured interval boundaries change. This is additive instrumentation, not proof that the clock writes are negligible.
- After `run()` synchronizes compute and copy streams, a single-group profile copies the stamp buffer device-to-host and accumulates it (`verify.cpp:1642-1651`). That post-run readback is extra work, but comes after the waits used to complete the window. It is not part of the instrumented graph's layer schedule. In the pipelined path, allocation of `prof_pin_` is attempted only under profiling (`verify.cpp:2494-2495`); if allocation fails, pipeline windows are left unprofiled. Where available, `fl_prof_` triggers an async stamp-buffer copy after graph launch (`verify.cpp:2585` onward). That introduces an extra transfer/command in the pipelined diagnostic route and is conditional on one group and pinned allocation.
- Profile accumulation/readback is guarded by `G==1` in ordinary run (`verify.cpp:1642`); the pipelined profiler likewise requires `G==1`. Two-group split windows are not fully profiled by this mechanism. Do not interpret missing output as zero work.
- `profile_report()` returns empty if disabled or no windows, and resets counters only after printing (`verify.cpp:1285-1308`). Reporting does not itself change the already completed window route.

These guards reveal one definite control-flow schedule change (`br` suppression) and several additive profile commands/copies. No numerical-path mutation was found in these profile guards, but source inspection alone does not prove bitwise equivalence or absence of timing/race effects. Existing route changes induced by the profile make even relative stage proportions questionable as estimates for quiet mode. Stamps also use a device counter with uncalibrated tick units on Xe, and their sequential differences can span graph intervals/overlap; ratios do not repair those limits.

## Quiet `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` receipt check

The control reads `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` during verifier initialization. If explicitly set, parsed nonzero means enabled, zero means disabled. If unset, the default is a runtime call to `graph_branch_pays(cs_, df_side_[0], df_side_[1])`; stream creation failure or exception disables it (`verify.cpp:398-418`). Thus a quiet receipt that merely omits the variable does not establish the effective value, because the default is runtime-measured. A receipt with an explicit value must also establish it reached this executable and matches this source/build before it can define the comparison.

The previously committed source-only R272 and R365 reports mention the instrumentation caveat and recommend profile-off quiet timing; they do not document an effective `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` value for the exact canonical quiet B570 decode seed. R401/v1 are research summaries, not safe proof of the flag's effective runtime value. I did not inspect live/active request records or the protected parent contract record, and did not search general environment state. Therefore this audit cannot say whether the current quiet seed actually has `df_branch_` true or false. No committed safe receipt examined here establishes that value. Do not run a new request or infer the default from the historical RTX/B70 comment.

## Interpretation and next comparison

The existing `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1` plus `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` route can expose its current bounded aggregate on ordinary serving, subject to clock support and successful profile output. It is useful only as a diagnostic characterization of the profile-mode route. To use it for a quiet-path hypothesis, first establish the matching quiet effective branch choice from an already committed safe receipt, then compare same-source, same-input quiet and profiled diagnostic runs with execution-mode labels and measure instrumentation perturbation. Even if the quiet branch was disabled, this paired comparison is still needed because of the extra stamp nodes and possible readback traffic.

No ratios here are quiet-path measurements, exclusive phase shares, critical-path fractions, or evidence toward 70 tok/s. To attribute the quiet path, use an instrumentation mechanism that preserves the branch decision (or make a separately reviewed diagnostic design that records and reports the decision without suppressing it), then quantify observer effect against unchanged quiet wall-time receipts. The existing profile's per-stage tick ratios alone cannot meet that requirement.

## Exact inspected source locations

- `src/core/verify.cpp:368-378` profile activation and fallback; `398-418` `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` parse/default; `499-506` `br` and stamp lambda; `674` fused-kernel profiling argument; `1285-1308` report/reset; `1642-1651` ordinary post-sync readback; `2494-2495,2585-2593` pipelined profile allocation and async readback.
- `src/kernels/xe/fused_gr.cpp:180,276-277,461-486,619,658` internal stamp-gated commands and dispatch.
- `src/program/generate.cpp:9717,10495-10518` ordinary serve diagnostics and report call.
- Prior source-only caveat: `research-native-decode-profile-clock-and-kernel-attribution-round272-v1.txt:32`; prior timing controls: `round365-xe-e32-critical-path-measurement-controls.txt:25,34`.
